about: Site sweep 1 of 3 (2026-11-06): the live site at https://orishamir.github.io/finance-tool/, at 1440x900 and at 390x844 with touch, checked against the visual and list rules (R1 to R24) of rules.json. Whole-page screenshots were read in screen-sized slices, and the DOM was measured for chart colours, columns the same on every row and repeated row text (sweep/sweep.mjs; the held goal and idle-cash pages were filled first with sweep/held.mjs). A break is what the founder would point at under that rule. Problems that an open GitHub issue already covers are under known. Colour distances are OKLab, times 100, computed from the theme's palette values.

breaks.what: The chart of money over time draws the money-market fund, the deposit and the savings plan as three teal lines in steps of one hue, so I cannot tell which line is which without the numbered circles.

The growth chart names its four parts (what is left, tax, management fees, your deposits) only in a legend above it and gives their amounts in a table below it; tax and fees are thin slivers on top with no figure on them. The same shared chart is on /guide/bank-deposit and /guide/brokerage-account.
On a phone the growth chart's tax and fee slivers are a few pixels thick, so the only way to read them is the table under the chart.
Only the top line carries its name and amount on the chart; the other three are named in a legend above and their amounts sit in a table below.
The current account chart labels its two lines at their ends and the gap on the band, then says the same again in a legend above and in three coloured tiles below.
The savings plan chart's legend shows two identical empty circles for 'locked' and 'not yet deposited', and the striped bars match neither, so I cannot tell what the striped bars are.
The hedging section's chart puts the unhedged and the hedged fund side by side as two bars a year, when the question is how far apart they are; the difference is only in the table under it.

A red note at the top says the site does not calculate any of these products, and then every card repeats a red locked 'not calculated' badge; the gold-price card also wears an amber 'according to the company' mark for the index owner's own description of its index.

Three of the seven product cards carry the same red 'not yet clear how it is taxed here' badge and the others show nothing, so the red warning is the loudest thing in the list of where I can hold the index.

Every track row repeats the words 'from savings' and 'from deposits', 'stocks' and 'foreign currency' with their colour dots, and '3 years' and '5 years', although the column heads already say them; the same shared row is on /tracks and every company page.

On a phone each track repeats six labels (from savings, from deposits, average yearly return, stocks, foreign currency, money managed), so the list of 143 tracks is mostly the same words over and over.

The company list is alphabetical inside its groups, so small managing companies (Infinity, Action, Globalnet, Slice) come before the banks everyone knows, which sit in a later group 'other banks and investment houses'.

known.what: The account list's fee bars carry no amounts on their parts; the legend now sits once at the foot of the list but the amounts are not on the bars.

In the account list's fee bars the account's fixed fee (red) and the buy-and-sell fee (orange) sit side by side on many rows and are close (7.3 normal, 3.2 under deuteranopia, against 15 and 8); red is also a status colour. The colour table was settled on 6 November and waits for the build.
The two cost bars of 'your choice' and 'the next pair' are two absolutes side by side; the result card's rebuild removes them, and the stairs with their three tables.
The fund list repeats the same labels (exposed to the dollar, accumulating, tax also on currency changes) on most rows of a group.
The fund list's 'against the index' column is to become the yearly cost the calculation counts.
Funds without a price carry two to three extra lines that priced rows lack.
Group-price lines under account rows wrap to two or three lines on a computer.
The two accounts that buy only abroad say 'no data' instead of what was read about each.
A 43 shekel winner gets the star inside the site's tie threshold, and the step chart reverses fund names with digits.
The two thin exposure rings inside each other look alike to a new reader.
'What would change the answer' is a list, not an analysis that compares everything at once.
The held 'what makes it different' visuals (issues 47 and 48) were not opened; they show only with ?review in the address.

notes: Every page was captured at both widths. /fees without a product shows only 'not found', so it has no visual to judge. The home page's goal form did not save a goal (the quick fields box-check.mjs fills are no longer on the home page); /indices/sp500 shows its result without one, and /goal/compare was reached by filling /goal.
The guide pages' 'what makes it different' visuals for three guides are held and were not opened with ?review.

Seen in passing, outside these rules: on a phone the indices fund chips and the guide calculators' input chips run off the screen's edge, the hedge year table overlaps (issue 193), and the company page of Interactive Israel shows 'all products 0' beside its one securities account.
